A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SQL-R1. Their complete main texts and appendices A–C are readable, including equations, tables, figures, case studies, and prompts. Renumbering and relocation can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original SQL-R1 benchmark evaluations, cold-start and reward ablations, candidate-rollout experiments, case studies, and training trajectories.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds Spider2.0 evaluation, difficulty-specific results, efficiency measurements, and reward-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The SFT and GRPO procedures, four reward components, training inputs, and self-consistency selection remain unchanged. The new reward-weight experiments test variants without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: v4 Table 4 adds evaluation on the Spider2.0 SQLite subset, extending coverage within NL2SQL. SynSQL training data, Spider, BIRD, and the three Spider variants remain. The new BIRD difficulty and efficiency analyses use retained coverage.

E2.justification: XiYan-SQL is newly evaluated in v4's BIRD efficiency comparison (Table 8). Existing comparator sets remain unchanged. GPT-4o and Deepseek-V3 in the new Spider2.0 table already appear in v2 Figure 2 and are not newly introduced comparison methods.

E3.justification: New evaluations report latency and tokens per question, compare greedy decoding with eight-candidate self-consistency, and test reward settings labeled 'Set to 1.0' and 'Increase by 50%' (v4 Tables 8 and 10). Existing training and inference settings remain unchanged; these are supplementary protocols.

E4.justification: v4 adds substantive analyses of whether model scaling particularly benefits difficult queries (B.1), accuracy versus inference cost (B.3), and sensitivity to reward magnitudes (B.6). These extend the questions investigated beyond v2's retained cold-start, component-removal, rollout, database-value, and case-study analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new 'statistical analysis' in B.1 reports difficulty-specific accuracies rather than uncertainty estimates. Training-trajectory reporting in Figure 10 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched existing results remain unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results in Tables 4, 6, 8, and 10: 20.0% Spider2.0 accuracy for SQL-R1-7B; 51.0%/56.5% challenging-query accuracy for 7B/14B; greedy versus self-consistency latency of 0.4/1.1 seconds with 63.7%/66.6% accuracy; and reward-sensitivity scores of 59.7–61.3%. These are new result entries, not performance improvements over matched v2 experiments.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective and reward definitions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs; the new sensitivity discussion is empirical interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about RL-based NL2SQL reasoning, synthetic-data training, cold-start strategies, accuracy, and interpretability. Added evaluations support existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations linking larger models' gains to complex-query dependencies, describing self-consistency's cost trade-off, and attributing reward sensitivity to potential reward hacking, instability, and verbosity. These extend explanatory discussion; the SQLite-dialect and base-model limitations in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a direct Hugging Face model-access link for SQL-R1-7B alongside the existing GitHub link. Existing implementation settings, hardware descriptions, preprocessing instructions, and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds the XiYan-SQL citation as reference 59 and positions SQL-R1 against it in the efficiency comparison. The existing references and Section 4 research positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely verbatim. Changes include an expanded B.1, new efficiency and sensitivity subsections, adjusted cross-references, and revised author-contact and conference-header text. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v4 adds four tables and places the new Spider2.0 table beside the narrowed reward-ablation table. Appendix tables are repositioned and renumbered, and reference spacing changes. Existing figures, case-study displays, and prompt layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies quantitative efficiency and reward-sensitivity evidence missing from v2, adds benchmark and difficulty-specific evaluation, and provides a model-access link. These modestly improve assessment and reuse. Benefits are tempered by sparse setup details, mechanism explanations exceeding the measurements, and unexplained baseline-total discrepancies: v4 Table 6 reports CodeS/DAIL-SQL at 58.5%/55.9%, while retained Table 1 gives 57.0%/54.8%.
